subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw require a live or deterministic stall reproduction before changing the processing/no-activeWorkKind stale-session recovery policy?
rationale: Current source proves the fallthrough and recovery scheduling, but current tests intentionally rely on that recovery behavior and the report labels the healthy-run abort chain as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this open for targeted live or deterministic evidence that a healthy active run reaches stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run during an event-loop stall before changing recovery semantics.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow state-aware classifier change and update tests, accepting the risk of redesigning stale processing recovery without live false-abort proof.

options.title: Fold into liveness cluster
options.body: Handle this together with the adjacent transcript I/O and stuck-session recovery reports so event-loop blocking and recovery policy are measured as one chain.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for targeted live or deterministic evidence that a healthy active run reaches stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run during an event-loop stall before changing recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent ownerless stalled-lane recovery work is closest to the policy choice around when recovery should observe, release, or abort.
